report.title: Silent session refresh — the living record
report.scope_note: Mid-execution snapshot: research and planning are locked, the auth store and silent-refresh path are in, and the session-expiry UX is blocked on OQ-1. Regenerated at each phase close; the manifest is canonical.
report.constraints: Never log refresh tokens or persist them in localStorage. Every auth flow must clear the security-review gate before merge. No third-party analytics on the token path.

stages.label: Refresh-strategy spike
stages.narrative: Compared silent refresh, refresh-on-focus, and prompt-on-expiry against the security constraint. Silent refresh with a bounded re-auth ceiling scored best on UX without widening token exposure.
stages.outcome: Silent refresh chosen as the default direction; expiry UX left open.

stages.label: Implementation plan
stages.narrative: Broke the work into three execute phases: (1) auth store + session model, (2) the silent-refresh transport, (3) the session-expiry UX. Validation closes the record.
stages.outcome: Three-phase plan approved at the plan gate.

stages.label: Auth store + session model
stages.narrative: Introduced a typed session store and moved the refresh token into an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie. The login shell now reads session state from the store rather than ad-hoc globals.
stages.outcome: Session model shipped behind the existing login screen; no user-visible change yet.

stages.label: Silent-refresh transport
stages.narrative: Building the background refresh: a single-flight refresh call that dedupes concurrent 401s, retries once, and hard-fails to the login route on rotation mismatch. Currently wiring the single-flight guard and its tests.
stages.deviations: Added a single-flight lock not in the original plan — concurrent tab refreshes were double-rotating the token.

stages.label: Session-expiry UX
stages.narrative: The user-facing behaviour when a silent refresh cannot recover. Blocked on OQ-1: silent drop to a re-auth modal, or an explicit 'session expired' interstitial.

stages.label: End-to-end validation
stages.narrative: Full auth E2E suite, the security-review gate, and captured screenshots of every expiry path before the feature report closes the record.

open_questions.question: When a silent refresh fails, should the session-expiry path drop silently to a re-auth modal, or show an explicit 'session expired' interstitial first?
open_questions.context: Blocks phase-3. The modal is faster but can surprise a user mid-task; the interstitial is clearer but adds a click.

channel.detail: Answer via `itt request answer <id>` or the op gate; the answer is folded in at the next phase close.

open_questions.question: What rotation window should the refresh token use?
open_questions.context: Raised while designing the cookie in phase-1.
open_questions.answer: A 7-day sliding window, revoked immediately on password change or explicit sign-out.

channel.detail: Answered in chat and recorded here.

decisions.decision: Refresh token uses a 7-day sliding window; revoke on password change and explicit sign-out.
decisions.rationale: Balances a low-friction return experience against the security constraint on token lifetime; revocation on credential change caps the blast radius.

decisions.decision: Store the refresh token in an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie — never in JS-reachable storage.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the token out of XSS reach and satisfies the report constraint against localStorage persistence.
alternatives: in-memory token with silent iframe refresh

items.note: Useful for tuning the rotation window, but out of scope until the UX ships and the token path is stable.

handoff.trigger: Re-enter once phase-3 ships and the silent-refresh path has a week of production data.
handoff.prompt: Scope first-party refresh-failure telemetry (counts and reason codes only, no token material) to tune the rotation window. Honor the no-third-party-analytics constraint on the token path.
